title: The 10 Best Gantry Cranes for Garages
subtitle: Portable adjustable gantry cranes for engines and heavy parts, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A gantry crane straddles the work, so you can lift an engine, transmission, or machine and roll it across the shop without an engine hoist's legs in the way. Amazon's portable gantries run from about $700 for a 3-ton frame to $1,600 for a 10.5-foot-wide kit with hoist. We ranked 10 on star rating, review volume, and features (included trolley, included hoist, published load test, locking casters, and a minimum height that fits under an 8-foot ceiling).

avoid.name: HUAGHEE Adjustable Gantry Crane, "1 Ton (2500Lbs)" Capacity, with Hoist and Trolley
avoid.verdict: It's a complete kit like the Yannivia, but the listing gives three different numbers for how much it can lift. The Yannivia 1-ton kit costs the same, states 2,000 lb, and backs it with a 1.5x load test.
reasons: The title says "1 Ton (2500Lbs)". One ton is 2,000 lb, not 2,500.
The first bullet cites a 3,300 lb factory test, which is 1.5 times 2,200 lb, a third capacity that matches neither the 1 ton nor the 2,500 lb figure.
On a crane you stand next to, the rated load is the one number you need to trust, and this listing doesn't give a consistent one.
Only two of the six casters lock, per the listing.

buyers_guide.a: An engine hoist is cheaper ($170 to $300) and folds away, but its legs have to roll under the car and its boom loses capacity as it extends. A gantry crane straddles the car or bench, lifts straight up on a trolley, and holds its full rating across the beam. Gantries are better for repeated lifts, heavy diesels, and moving parts across the shop.

buyers_guide.q: Will it fit in my garage?
buyers_guide.a: Check the minimum height first. Most 3-ton gantries here start at 8.53 ft, too tall for a standard 8 ft garage ceiling. The JEGS (7 ft 11 in.) and both Yannivia kits (7.65 and 7.78 ft) are built to fit under 8 ft. Remember the hoist and chain hang below the beam, so your lift height is less than the crane height.

buyers_guide.q: Frame only or a complete kit?
buyers_guide.a: Frame-only gantries need a trolley (which rides the I-beam) and a chain hoist, bought separately. The Yannivia and LYFOO kits include both, plus slings and shackles. BSMTEK, Dkenicor, LDHTHOPI, and VEVOR include a trolley on some listings but not a hoist.

buyers_guide.q: How much capacity do I need?
buyers_guide.a: A 1-ton (2,000 lb) gantry handles most car engines and transmissions. Diesels, truck engines with transmissions attached, and machine tools call for 2 to 3 tons. Keep the hoist and trolley ratings at or above the frame's rating; the system is only as strong as its weakest part.

buyers_guide.q: Can I move it with a load on it?
buyers_guide.a: If the manual allows moving under load at all, keep it to short moves on smooth, level concrete with the load low and centered. Lock the casters before lifting, and never roll a loaded gantry over cracks, expansion joints, or slopes.
